austronesian-peoples.name: Austronesian peoples
austronesian-peoples.summary: Peoples descended from a prehistoric seaborne migration out of Taiwan around 3000–1500 BCE, who used sails and outrigger boats to spread across the Indo-Pacific, from Madagascar to Easter Island and New Zealand.

ancient-hawaii.name: Ancient Hawaii
ancient-hawaii.summary: The period of Hawaiian history before the 1795 founding of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi by Kamehameha the Great, settled by Polynesian voyagers and marked by fishponds, farming and stone temples.

polynesian-dog.name: Polynesian Dog
polynesian-dog.summary: Now-extinct varieties of domesticated dog kept in Polynesia for companionship and food, wiped out by crossbreeding after European dogs arrived; DNA links them to Southeast Asian dogs.

aleurites-moluccanus.name: Kukui (candlenut tree)
aleurites-moluccanus.summary: A tropical tree, also called candlenut, first described by Linnaeus in 1753; its nut has various regional uses, such as being ground into a condiment in traditional Hawaii.

ancient-hawaiian-aquaculture.name: Taro fishponds
ancient-hawaiian-aquaculture.summary: Shallow, walled ponds built by Hawaiians before European contact to raise fish such as mullet, considered the most advanced fish-farming among Pacific peoples; over 360 existed by Captain Cook's arrival.

lapita-culture.name: Lapita culture
lapita-culture.summary: A Neolithic Austronesian people who settled Island Melanesia by sea around 1600 to 500 BCE, known for distinctive stamped pottery and ancestral to Polynesian, Micronesian and Melanesian peoples.

ng-s-n-culture.name: Đông Sơn culture
ng-s-n-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture centered on the Red River Delta in northern Vietnam, flourishing from about 1000 BC to the first century AD, known for wet-rice farming and skilled bronze casting, including the famous Đông Sơn drums.

australo-melanesian.name: Australo-Melanesian
australo-melanesian.summary: An outdated grouping term for various peoples indigenous to Melanesia and Australia, once used in now-discredited racial classification schemes.

marquesas-islands.name: Marquesas Islands
marquesas-islands.summary: Volcanic island group in French Polynesia, settled around the 10th century AD by voyagers from West Polynesia and named after a 16th-century Spanish viceroy of Peru.

cook-islands.name: Cook Islands
cook-islands.summary: A self-governing Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific, in free association with New Zealand, made up of 15 islands with its capital at Avarua on Rarotonga.

proto-polynesian-language.name: Proto-Polynesian language
proto-polynesian-language.summary: The reconstructed ancestor of all Polynesian languages, believed to have originated in the Tonga and Samoa area, itself descended from Proto-Oceanic.

m-ui.name: Māui
m-ui.summary: A trickster culture hero of Polynesian mythology, credited across the Pacific with feats such as stealing fire, fishing up islands and slowing the sun.

ulupoka.name: Ulupoka
ulupoka.summary: God of evil and demons in Fijian and Polynesian mythology, beheaded by other gods in a great battle but unable to die; his wandering body still causes death and misfortune.

hina-goddess.name: Hina
hina-goddess.summary: A name for various Polynesian goddesses, usually a powerful female figure with dominion over a specific domain, appearing across many Pacific island cultures.

sina-and-the-eel.name: Sina
sina-and-the-eel.summary: A female figure of Polynesian mythology, also known as Hina, appearing across island traditions as a goddess or ancestress alongside figures like Māui.

atua.name: Atua
atua.summary: Polynesian word for "power" or "strength," used for the gods and spirits of peoples such as the Māori and Hawaiians, originating in pre-Christian myths and legends.

rangi-and-papa.name: Rangi and Papa
rangi-and-papa.summary: The primal Sky and Earth couple of Māori mythology's creation story, whose union is said to give rise to the world and the Māori people.

tangaroa.name: Tangaroa
tangaroa.summary: Great god of the sea, lakes, rivers and their creatures, including fish, in Māori mythology, who also controls the tides and is sometimes depicted as a whale.

society-islands.name: Society Islands
society-islands.summary: An archipelago in Polynesia in the South Pacific, part of French Polynesia, whose largest island is Tahiti; settlers from here later helped populate other Pacific islands.

patrick-vinton-kirch.name: Patrick Vinton Kirch
patrick-vinton-kirch.summary: American archaeologist and professor emeritus at UC Berkeley, former curator and director of the Phoebe A. Hearst Museum of Anthropology, later a professor at the University of Hawai'i Manoa and a Bishop Museum board member.

mana-oceanic-cultures.name: Mana
mana-oceanic-cultures.summary: In Melanesian and Polynesian belief, a supernatural force thought to permeate the universe and be held by any person, object or place, seen as something to be cultivated rather than a source of power in itself.

tapu-polynesian-culture.name: Tapu
tapu-polynesian-culture.summary: A Polynesian concept of something holy or sacred involving rules and prohibitions; the source of the English word "taboo", from Captain Cook's 1777 visit to Tonga.

proto-oceanic-language.name: Proto-Oceanic language
proto-oceanic-language.summary: The reconstructed common ancestor of the Oceanic branch of Austronesian languages, likely spoken in the late 2nd millennium BCE by the Lapita culture near Papua New Guinea.

teouma.name: Teouma
teouma.summary: An archaeological site on Efate island in Vanuatu holding the oldest known cemetery in the Pacific Islands, linked to the Lapita people of the ninth and tenth centuries BC.

efate.name: Efate
efate.summary: Island in Vanuatu's Shefa Province, home to the country's capital, Port Vila.

bismarck-archipelago.name: Bismarck Archipelago
bismarck-archipelago.summary: A group of islands off the northeastern coast of New Guinea, part of Papua New Guinea, covering about 50,000 square kilometres.

haveke-language.name: Haveke
haveke-language.summary: An endangered Kanak language of New Caledonia, with only about 300 speakers reported in 1982 and virtually no children learning it since.

mana-skeleton.name: Mana (skeleton)
mana-skeleton.summary: The best-preserved skeleton of a Lapita-age woman ever found, and the oldest skeleton discovered in Fiji, dating to about 800 BCE, later given a computer-modeled facial reconstruction.
